questions.question: Explain, step by step, how the natural greenhouse effect keeps the Earth warm.
questions.expected_answer: Sunlight (mainly visible light) passes through the atmosphere and is absorbed by the ground and oceans, which warm up. The warm surface gives off infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases (water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide) let sunlight through but absorb some of the infrared radiation, warm up and re-emit it in all directions, partly back to the surface. This keeps the surface about 33 °C warmer than without it (about 15 °C instead of about −18 °C).

questions.question: Distinguish between the greenhouse effect and the enhanced greenhouse effect, and name two human activities responsible for the enhanced effect.
questions.expected_answer: The greenhouse effect is the natural warming of the Earth by greenhouse gases and is essential for life. The enhanced greenhouse effect is the strengthening of this effect because human activities have increased greenhouse gas concentrations, causing global warming. Activities: burning fossil fuels (coal in power stations, petrol/diesel in vehicles), deforestation, livestock farming (methane), landfills, fertiliser use.

questions.question: Describe two possible effects of global warming on South Africa and two ways South Africans can reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.expected_answer: Effects (any two): more frequent/severe droughts and water shortages (e.g. Cape Town 2015-2018); more intense floods (e.g. KZN 2022); heat waves; rising sea level threatening coastal cities; lower crop yields; loss of biodiversity in fynbos/Karoo; coral bleaching. Reductions (any two): solar and wind power instead of coal; saving electricity and using efficient appliances/LEDs; solar water heaters; public transport, walking, cycling; reducing waste; planting and protecting trees and grasslands.
